precepts.text: I take not this my sister for lust, but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together. We pray we see our older years together. Some of us make it there and some do not; let it be because of passing, not because you would not apply the scriptures. precepts.point: Those of you married a long time are supposed to still be able to look at your wife or your husband and see when you were young. That is why people who have that can be content: as you get older, both of you change, both of you get old, but you remember. Let her breast satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love. Her body will change with the years, but she is yours, brother, and that bond cannot be broken if you are in the Lord.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
Marriage was designed to happen when you are young: you meet a young woman, and this is the person you grow old with. “rejoice with the wife of thy youth.” Tobias prayed the same thing on his wedding night: “And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.”

Hands went up around the room for five, ten, fifteen, twenty and twenty-five years of marriage and more, and the Bishop has been married 36 years. These are the examples we have right here. Those married a long time are supposed to still be able to look at their wife or husband and see when they were young. That is why they can be content: both of you change, both of you get old, but you remember.

“let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.” When you marry her young her breasts are at three o'clock; as you grow old together they will be at six. But they are yours, brother, no matter what time it is. You walk in the room and she is the only thing you see. That bond can't be broken if you are in the Lord.

So we pray we are able to see our older years together. Some of us make it there and some don't; let it be because of passing, not because you weren't applying the scriptures or listening in class. The prophecy classes are dope, but you have to have the same zeal for the classes on marriage and repentance and apply them in your everyday life. Otherwise your marriage falls apart, your kids go who knows where, and then you look at us like it was our fault.

precepts.text: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, for that is thy portion. There is your romance, part of the aging, and it is a commandment; we are here seventy or eighty years at best.
precepts.point: He took her uprightly and they aged together mercifully, and with age comes beauty, love, and passion, not whimsical movie feelings. Stop chasing a feeling; get your mind like Tobit's. If even a majority of families moved in that spirit, how much stronger are we as a people for the time of trouble to come. Weddings are not done here for anyone who has not proved for three years.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Tobias prayed, “mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.” To age together is the long, intertwined journey of partners growing old side by side: shared history, mutual support through life's changes, companionship, and facing life's challenges as a team. Aged means refined, like wine or cheese.

Then Solomon: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity”. There's your romance. Live joyfully: that's part of the aging. “all the days of the life of thy vanity”, because we are here just for a fleeting moment, seventy or eighty years at best. All the days God gives you, you should live joyfully with your wife. That's a commandment.

“for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” This is how things are supposed to be set up. If you want to navigate this world the right way, you have to navigate your marriage this way.

So the joy is not the foundation; it grows out of it. Everything else has to be established first, or the romance will be fleeting and break the foundation of the scriptures. Tobias took his wife uprightly, and the living joyfully comes in the aging together.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
You want passion in the relationship? Here it is: “Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth. Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.”

Ravished is not a regular word: it means to fill someone with intense delight and rapture. Delight, charm, enthral, captivate, spellbind, bewitch, fascinate. That goes into the power a woman has in her voice and her conversation. There's your passion, there's your romance, after the foundation of your marriage is set up correctly and you age together.

But that can't exist if the other, divine parts of the marriage are not set up correctly; it's not going to happen. You don't seek this first. It's like looking for furniture, things for the walls, carpet and rugs, when you haven't even bought the house yet and don't know if the walls will hold or the foundation is strong. That's how we treat marriage nowadays.

Tobias did it in the right order: “I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly”. The being ravished always with her love comes after that foundation, as the fruit of it.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Tobias prayed, and Sara “said with him, Amen.” She agreed, because her mind was on her lord; she didn't say, wait, what about the house, what about the gifts. Sirach gives more insight into the character that strengthens marriage: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

A man and a wife that agree together. The agreement is not that you both like the same music, the same colors, the same food; that's part of the aging stuff. The agreement is this: she agrees to follow the scriptures that pertain to her as a wife, whether or not there are contingencies, because the Bible gives no contingencies for a wife's behavior. You do or you don't. And he agrees to do the same as a husband.

You agree in God that you are going to follow his order of marriage, running it with your responsibilities as a wife and yours as a husband the way the Bible says. That is what is beautiful in God's eyes, because it will work the way he intended when you do those things.

precepts.text: Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be doubled. A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all, but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all. Honour is measured against what the scripture says. A man experiences love through respect, sincere and innate, not remembered and forced; if you have to remind yourself to respect your husband, you are not in submission.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.” Virtuous deals with her character. Look how everything gets better in the marriage when the wife moves in that spirit; a virtuous wife brings peace. Tobias asked God that he and his wife might become aged together, and a virtuous wife doubles those days.

“A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.” She honors him by agreeing to follow what the Lord says; that's the honor. A woman that honors her husband equals wisdom for the woman. But not how you think: you measure it against the scripture and ask, am I fulfilling all of these things? Pride is what breaks the submission.

When Titus says to teach the women to love their husbands, we have taken it for years as surface emotions. A man experiences love through respect; that is the chief love language of a man. Why does he like being around the brothers so much? Because he's respected among his peers. If the wife reverences him, he'll feel the love, and everything else falls into place behind it.

And not forced respect. It has to come from a sincere place. If you have to remember and remind yourself to respect your husband, you're not in submission. If you really desire your husband and see him as he is, not through a warped worldly view, it will come out of you innately, and watch what will come out of him innately.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Tobias prayed, “Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay”, and “let us make unto him an aid like unto himself.” Sirach says the same: “He that getteth a wife beginneth a possession, a help like unto himself, and a pillar of rest.”

Marriage describes partnership and support, plain and simple. Not a rom-com romantic movie, not a novella or a soap opera. A help like unto himself, a pillar of rest.

What do you see in those words? Stability and wisdom over emotional intensity. We have to stop emphasizing the wrong thing. The emotional intensity comes as a byproduct of those things.

The Bible shows men taking wives: he took a wife, he got a possession. That is the foundation Tobias laid in his prayer, a helper and stay from whom came mankind, a nation, and it is what we must get back to.

precepts.text: The prayer of the marriage bed: mercifully ordain that we may become aged together; that is the prayer, not a vow.
precepts.point: Marriage is not sin, but such shall have trouble in the flesh; trials will come up in a marriage that have to be fixed with the scriptures, so ask the Most High for the mercy and the strength to endure rather than vowing what you cannot uphold.

note.label: Numbers 30: The Law of Vows

precepts.why:
On the wedding day we do not make vows in the manner of Christianity, promising things the flesh may not perform. We pray as Tobias and Sara prayed. “Then began Tobias to say, Blessed art thou, O God of our fathers, and blessed is thy holy and glorious name for ever; let the heavens bless thee, and all thy creatures.”

“Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: thou hast said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make unto him an aid like unto himself. And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together. And she said with him, Amen.”

That is the prayer of the marriage bed, not a vow: that the Lord mercifully ordain that husband and wife may become aged together. We apply the scriptures to the marriage instead of binding the soul with an oath.

precepts.text: Marriage is taking a sister of thine own people, not for lust but uprightly, to become aged together.

Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: thou hast said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make unto him an aid like unto himself. And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.”

That is marriage: taking a sister of thine own people, not for lust but uprightly, to become aged together. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life, and if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with.

The nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how “they will turn away thy son from following me”. A wife of thine own people keeps the house in the covenant.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why:
“And when they had supped, they brought Tobias in unto her.” He remembered the words of Raphael and made a smoke with the heart and the liver of the fish, and when the evil spirit smelled it, “he fled into the utmost parts of Egypt, and the angel bound him.” Sara could not be married because an evil spirit would kill the men she laid with, and the angel Raphael told Tobias what to do.

Then in the wedding chamber, “Tobias rose out of the bed, and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray that God would have pity on us.” This is what to get to. He blessed the God of our fathers: “Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: thou hast said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make unto him an aid like unto himself.” It is not good that man be alone, because then you start looking at other men, you start looking at the animals.

“And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust.” Brothers, a lot of you take a woman for lust. Ask a brother his type and it is based on some lust he saw on the internet: some high yellow thick-bodied hoe called Pinky, and he is going to wait for a woman like that to come into IUIC. You stupid as hell, ruining your whole life over a lust. I like Beyoncé; Beyoncé ain’t coming up in here. A lot of them actors make covenants with the devil. And the sisters: I want Idris Elba, I want Chris Brown, women destroying their whole marriage to go on stage and kiss that knucklehead. Of course you have to have a natural draw to your spouse, but if it is just lust and nothing else to it, don’t marry her.

“But uprightly”: according to the law of Moses. “Therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.” If you can’t see yourself growing old with that sister, don’t marry her. You got to envision it in your mind when old age comes: black people’s skin sags at times, the sisters get that fupa after the babies, the brothers get a big pot belly. You got to know you can deal with that.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why: “And he kept the wedding feast fourteen days.” The wedding feast at the marriage lasted fourteen days.

note.label: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

precepts.why:
Her father said “he should take the half of his goods, and go in safety to his father; and should have the rest when I and my wife be dead.” I want all you men to listen: her father gave him half of his goods to make sure his daughter was taken care of, and the son-in-law would get the rest when the father and mother were dead. Everybody wants a dowry, but nobody wants to read the verse where the father gave half his goods to the son-in-law for his daughter.

You brothers with daughters, you better have a clause, because some brothers will just get there, see what they can get, take half and be gone. That is why you have trust funds and things like that.

note.label: THE REBIRTH OF GOD’S NATION ON THE EARTH

precepts.why:
These are the scriptures that tell what she brings to his bones. “The grace of a wife delighteth her husband”: a wife, not a jump-off, not a hoe. “And her discretion will fatten his bones”: she is not stupid. He lights up, he’s happy; she is adding years to his life. That is what you should be thinking about when you look for a wife. You come to her father and ask for her hand, and the father checks you all the way out; if he finds you worthy, you had better take care of her.

“A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord.” She is not going to be silent if the bills aren’t paid, or if you are battling four or five women. She may be tricked into thinking she is all right, but inside she is mad as hell. You can’t treat her like garbage.

“And there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed.” Ponder that. When you see married men do great things, what do other men say? He must have a good woman behind him: she fattens his bones. Her daddy taught her well, and the people she came up around taught her well. That is what you want by your side, brothers, a wife to grow aged together with.

points: The pattern so far: Adam and Eve, divine creation and order; Abraham and Sarah, covenant and mission; Isaac and Rebekah, ordained and then love; Jacob and Rachel, attraction and complication. The Bible rarely describes the beauty of wives; Rebekah is known for hospitality and faith, Zipporah's looks are never mentioned, and Elisabeth is called righteous. Sarah's beauty is mentioned only for external threats. Proverbs 31 never says her price is above rubies because she is a baddie. Social media validates sisters with likes and breeds a subtle vanity; be presentable, but do not put status on appearance.

Tobias rose out of the bed and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray. Blessed art thou, O God of our fathers; thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind. That is the foundation, a nation. His brief prayer speaks volumes about what Tobit taught him; married or unmarried, meditate on these words and do not let them fall.

points: Y’all don’t think Abraham and Sarah argued? Oh yes, they argued. Sarah was unhappy at times: she couldn’t have no kids, and her servant Hagar was mocking her. Tobit’s wife Anna was unhappy when her son didn’t come home for a while.

A sister divorced her husband over a damn dog. A brother from the island, and Caribbean brothers don’t want a dog in the house, told her, if we get married you got to get rid of the dog. She said okay, they got married, he came home from work and stepped in it, and now they’re fighting, and she says ‘I want a divorce, I’m not happy’, over a dog. Some of you women are stupid as hell. Then there’s the one at home in the bed with her husband who gets a message, tells him she has to get the baby some milk, goes to the nigga’s house, comes back all sweaty without a shower, and throws the baby on her sweaty titty, and forgot the milk. And the weak man goes ‘I want to keep her, she my wife’: brother, you get your simple self out of here too, you ain’t a man of God. Some of you weak men and you evil sisters, just go.

“And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust”: he didn’t just take her for sex reasons. Some of you marry for lust, because she got a pretty face, big breasts and a big booty. All that fades in time: the breasts start to come around the knees and swing, the booty starts to hang; some sisters got five bras on trying to hold them things up. There’s nothing wrong with liking that, but that’s what happens in time. Time changes things, brothers too.

“But uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.” That’s what the sister in the world was talking about: becoming aged together. A sister in the world got to tell some of you sisters that that’s what marriage is about. You’re going to have your ups and downs in marriage; it’s inevitable. The Apostle Paul warned you that you will have trouble in the flesh, and some of you like to close your ears to it: financial, sexual, health, extended family. Some of you are too attached to extended family, and some of you are too attached to the world and want to keep doing worldly things.

A husband wanted to take his wife to a bar, and the wife said, look, I don’t want to go there, we’re the only people sitting there with fringes and a border of blue. Bro, your wife is telling you she don’t want to go there because she feels uncomfortable around sinners.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind.” When a man and a woman come together, they have the ability to produce gods. That is not some plaything; you can’t have children without a wife. She is not something to run through and treat like garbage. How would a father feel, after all the trouble of raising her up, seeing his daughter treated like a piece of meat?

Of them two came mankind: man and woman have the ability to produce the whole planet. As Officer Eli brought out on the Bible Book of Our Fathers, eight people were on the ark, Noah, his three sons and their wives, and from them the whole earth was peopled. That is how special those women were. Do it right once and righteous sons and daughters come of it: two or three children marry, five or six families become 12, then 24. Women, understand your value. If your camp is not teaching you that, get the hell out; and brothers, if the sisters don’t want the right thing, get up and go, because some women are as nasty as some men.

“It is not good that man should be alone”: that is back to let them marry. “Let us make unto him an aid like unto himself.” When you marry you are looking for an aid that can actually help you, not a jump-off: one who values what you bring and values that family and that child. And you don’t treat her like a piece of meat.

note.label: THE REBIRTH OF GOD’S NATION ON THE EARTH

points: “And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly.” Anything outside of what we just read is taking her for lust, and that is exactly what this multiple-women situation is about: whoredom. Uprightly means taking care of her in all the things she needs. A lot of these brothers have no money to take care of anything; we are in captivity. You can’t handle four or five women, and she’s dumb to say he can hold her down. He has no discipline to deal right with her; he’ll go dipping into something else and bring back a disease, with no paperwork, nothing to keep anyone straight.

“Therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.” When you look at that sister you are proving, do you think about her getting grey hairs, getting old with you? The young hot brothers often don’t. As soon as she changes a little, or he does, he ain’t satisfying me, she can’t do it like what I’ve seen on porn, and then they want counsel. We ain’t running that type of mess.

note.label: THE REBIRTH OF GOD’S NATION ON THE EARTH

points: “And she said with him, Amen.” Amen means she is in agreement with you, and you with what you are supposed to do as a married couple. No separation. The father gave you the woman to take care of her: I took care of her as a father, now you pick it up. We don’t want to hear any craziness after all the work her father put in.

note.label: THE REBIRTH OF GOD’S NATION ON THE EARTH

points: “So they slept both that night.” They had a perfect understanding. They were righteously married; he was not taking her for lust but saw her as his helpmeet, to help him make it to old age together. They woke up and praised the Most High, and that was the beginning of their life: a journey together, she on your team.

In that union the family and children come, building a nation together, she your helpmeet and you her guide. Challenges will come, bills and such, but because you came together properly you will help each other through the trial. What God has joined together, let not man, sin, lust for other women, or adultery when age sets in put asunder. Wanting somebody younger is all lust. Every man must have his own wife and every wife her own husband. You are supposed to love what is between her ears more than what is between her legs. A beautiful woman cheers the countenance, but nobody wants a pretty dummy.
